note: THE THREE RESERVED ART REGIONS. No art exists yet and none is generated, bought or downloaded by this unit — these are EMPTY reserved regions. The durable decision recorded here is the ASPECT RATIO, not the picture: whatever shape a region is, is the shape every future piece of art must be drawn to, and changing it after the art exists means the art is redrawn. Adding art later must be a change to `source` in this file and nothing else. See docs/ART-BIBLE.md §3 and §4b.

slots.label: Scenery
slots.why: 16:9 is not a preference — docs/ART-BIBLE.md §3 already LOCKS the five floor backdrops at 16:9 with a deep-shadow bottom third. Any other shape here would invalidate an art brief that predates this unit, so the region is drawn to the spec rather than the spec to the region. It ships on the hub, which is the floor's own screen, mounted in the READING column above the prose as an establishing shot. CORRECTED 2026-09-09: it used to be capped by WIDTH ALONE (in screens.css), and that starved the narration - 440px of width is 247px of height whatever the window is, so at the 960x640 minimum the frame took 247 of the reading column's 550 and the prose measured zero pixels. The cap now lives with the container (#scenery .void-art-slot in game.css) and caps BOTH directions, 440px wide and 22vh tall, with this ratio governing inside the box. THE RATIO ITSELF IS UNCHANGED AND IS NOT AVAILABLE AS A FIX for a layout problem: it is the commitment every future backdrop is drawn to.

slots.label: Enemy
slots.why: Upright, because the subject is a standing figure and a wide frame would crop it or strand it in empty air. 3:4 is the SHALLOWEST upright ratio that still reads as a portrait, and shallow is what its first placement needed: it shipped in the fixed 220px HUD column beside the foe's own vitals, where at the column's 140px cap 3:4 was 187px of height (2:3 would have been 210px, 9:16 249px). MOVED 2026-09-12 by docs/PLAN.md #6: the region is now the centre of the battle screen's framed stage (#arena in desktop.html, battle.css), centred and capped at 32vh of HEIGHT with its width following from the ratio - about 205px tall and 154px wide at the 960x640 minimum, so the narration keeps its floor below the frame. THE RATIO SURVIVED THE MOVE UNCHANGED, as it was committed to: the same shape in a wider place, and the shape a future sprite (#7) is drawn to.

slots.label: Character
slots.why: Square, and it is the one ratio here chosen for the layout as much as for the subject. The player portrait lives in the fixed 220px HUD column, where game.css caps a slot at 140px wide — so 1:1 reserves 140px of column height and 3:4 would reserve 187px. Those 47px are part of what decides whether the column scrolls at the 960x640 minimum. (Until docs/PLAN.md #6 a battle stacked the enemy's region in this column too; the fight is now its own framed stage, and the HUD column is hidden while it runs.) The vitals are not what pays either way: both regions render BELOW HP, XP and the condition chips, and #sheet scrolls. It also tells the art brief something true: this is a chest-up crop, not a full figure.
